papers.title: Advance care planning and care coordination for people with parkinsonism: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Parkinsonism comprises a group of progressive neurodegenerative disorders, including Parkinson's disease and atypical parkinsonism. In advanced stages, advance care planning (ACP) and coordinated care are important to align treatment with patients' values and reduce unwanted interventions and caregiver burden. In this study we evaluated whether a nurse-led intervention increases documentation of end-of-life preferences and improves patient and caregiver outcomes. In this multicentre, single-blind randomized controlled trial (2020-2022), participants with parkinsonism (Hoehn & Yahr stage ≥3) and their caregivers were included across seven neurology centres in Austria, Estonia, Germany, Greece, Italy, Sweden, and the UK. Participants were randomized 1:1 to either the PD_Pal intervention (a structured six-month nurse-led ACP and care coordination program) or usual care. The primary outcome was documentation of end-of-life preferences at six months. A total of 189 people with parkinsonism and 189 family caregivers were enrolled. No significant difference was found in documentation of end-of-life preferences between groups (P = 0.77). Caregivers in the intervention group reported improved quality of life at six months (P = 0.03), although this effect was not sustained at 12 months. No differences were observed in other outcomes. These findings highlight challenges in implementing ACP in advanced parkinsonism and the need for flexible, stage-appropriate strategies.

papers.title: Brain penetration of benserazide inversely associates with levodopa response in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Levodopa combined with a peripheral DOPA decarboxylase inhibitor (DDCI) is the first-line treatment for Parkinson's disease (PD), yet interindividual response variability remains poorly understood. Whether DDCIs penetrate the central nervous system (CNS) in the context of potential blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction in PD and influence levodopa efficacy is unclear. We therefore assessed CNS exposure of benserazide (BZ) and its active metabolite 2,3,4-trihydroxybenzylhydrazine (THBH) and their association with levodopa response. Fifteen PD patients (Hoehn-Yahr 2-3) underwent a standardized levodopa challenge test and were classified as good (≥50% improvement) or poor responders. Paired blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples were collected after a single oral dose of levodopa/BZ (200/50 mg), and analyte concentrations were quantified using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography with electrochemical detection (UPLC-ECD). Both BZ and THBH were detectable in CSF, indicating BBB penetration. CSF concentrations and CSF-to-plasma ratios of total BZ (BZ + THBH) were significantly higher in poor responders (p = 0.021 and 0.014, respectively) and negatively correlated with levodopa efficacy (p = 0.034 and 0.008, respectively). papers.title: Characterization of blood metabolomic responses to deep brain stimulation in patients with Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) constitutes one of the few therapeutic strategies for advanced Parkinson's disease. Although DBS causes rapid alterations in neuronal metabolism, whether it remodels the circulating metabolome and thereby alleviates systemic symptoms remains unknown. Here, we used high-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry to perform untargeted plasma metabolomics of plasma samples from patients with Parkinson's disease pre- and post-DBS to profile transient metabolic alterations in plasma that could be attributed to DBS. Numerous metabolites involved in tyrosine metabolism-including dopamine, phenylacetaldehyde, 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde, and tyrosine-were reduced in abundance following DBS. In contrast, metabolites such as lactate were increased in abundance in response to DBS. We further characterized metabolites associated with the immediate therapeutic effects of DBS and identified acrylic acid level as a potential metabolic predictor of long-term prognosis. Collectively, our findings provide important insights into DBS-induced reprogramming of the plasma metabolome.

papers.title: Abatacept-Associated behavioral, inflammatory, and immunohistochemical changes in a rotenone-induced rat model of parkinsonism.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neuroinflammation and peripheral immune dysregulation are implicated in Parkinson's disease, supporting evaluation of immunomodulatory interventions. We investigated outcomes associated with abatacept administered before rotenone exposure, alone or combined with L-DOPA/benserazide administered concurrently with rotenone, in a rat model of parkinsonism. METHODS AND RESULTS: Thirty male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to five groups: control, rotenone, rotenone plus abatacept, rotenone plus L-DOPA/benserazide, and combined treatment. Rotenone and L-DOPA/benserazide were administered concurrently for 14 days; abatacept was administered twice, beginning 48 h before rotenone. Motor performance and serum IL-10 and TNF-α were assessed. TH and pSer129 α-synuclein immunopositivity in the substantia nigra and pSer129 α-synuclein and TNF-α immunopositivity in peripheral tissues were evaluated semi-quantitatively. Compared with rotenone, abatacept increased rearing, ambulation, and serum IL-10 and decreased serum TNF-α, without significantly altering rotarod performance or nigral immunopositivity. L-DOPA improved all motor measures and increased serum IL-10 but did not significantly alter serum TNF-α or nigral immunopositivity. Combined treatment improved all motor measures, increased serum IL-10 and nigral TH immunopositivity, decreased serum TNF-α, and reduced pSer129 α-synuclein immunopositivity in four peripheral tissues and TNF-α immunopositivity in the liver and jejunum. Serum TNF-α was lower with abatacept than with L-DOPA. Compared with L-DOPA, combined treatment additionally affected only ambulation and serum TNF-α. papers.title: Recombinant AAV-Based Gene Therapy for Central Nervous System Disorders: From Gene Replacement to Precision Editing and Circuit Modulation.
papers.abstract: Recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) vectors have moved central nervous system (CNS) gene therapy from experimental proof of concept to clinically validated treatment, yet therapeutic design remains highly dependent on disease mechanism, cellular distribution, and treatment timing. This narrative review examines recent progress in rAAV-based interventions for neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) and neurodegenerative disorders. For monogenic NDDs, gene replacement is most applicable to loss-of-function conditions with compatible payload size and tolerable expression, whereas dominant-negative, gain-of-function, and dosage-sensitive disorders may require allele-selective silencing or precise DNA or RNA editing. Rett syndrome illustrates both the reversibility of postnatal dysfunction and the need for tightly regulated transgene expression. Spinal muscular atrophy provides the leading translational paradigm: rAAV9-mediated SMN1 replacement demonstrates the value of early diagnosis, adequate tissue exposure, and treatment before irreversible neuronal loss. For complex neurodegenerative diseases, emerging strategies extend beyond simple gene addition. APOE-directed editing and protective-variant replacement may enable genotype-informed intervention in Alzheimer's disease, whereas Parkinson's disease programs combine restoration of dopamine synthesis, neuroprotection, and genetically encoded circuit modulation. Across these indications, major barriers include incomplete and nonselective CNS delivery, immune and dose-related toxicity, limited redosing, durable control of transgene or editor activity, off-target effects, and uncertain translation from animal models to humans. Progress over the next decade will depend on human-compatible vectors, cell-selective and regulatable expression, rigorous long-term safety assessment, biomarker-guided trials, and rational combinations that connect molecular target engagement to meaningful neurological benefit.

papers.title: PINK1‑regulated mitophagy dysfunction in the pathogenesis of Parkinson's disease (Review).
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder, characterized by the progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra and the accumulation of misfolded α‑synuclein forming Lewy bodies. Emerging evidence highlights mitochondrial dysfunction as an important and early event in PD pathogenesis. Among the key regulators of mitochondrial quality control, PTEN‑induced kinase 1 (PINK1) plays a pivotal role by initiating mitophagy, the selective clearance of damaged mitochondria. Under physiological conditions, PINK1 is rapidly degraded, whereas mitochondrial depolarization stabilizes PINK1 on the outer mitochondrial membrane, where it recruits and activates Parkin, an E3 ubiquitin ligase, to promote mitophagy. Loss‑of‑function mutations in PINK1 also disrupt this process, leading to the accumulation of dysfunctional mitochondria, oxidative stress, abnormal calcium homeostasis and neuronal apoptosis. Furthermore, PINK1 deficiency has been shown to exacerbate α‑synuclein aggregation, impair synaptic transmission and activate neuroinflammatory pathways, collectively accelerating dopaminergic neurodegeneration. Therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring or enhancing PINK1‑mediated mitophagy through pharmacological activation, gene delivery or modulation of parallel pathways‑represent a promising avenue for PD intervention. Continued elucidation of the molecular functions of PINK1 will provide critical insights into mitochondrial homeostasis and novel therapeutic targets for PD.

papers.title: Effect of a multidisciplinary intensive outpatient rehabilitation program on plasma neurofilaments and myokines in Parkinson's disease: an exploratory analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Physical exercise is increasingly recognized as a supportive intervention for people with Parkinson's disease (PwPD), yet the biological mechanisms underlying its effects remain unclear. This study investigated whether exercise-based rehabilitation modulates circulating biomarkers associated with neuroaxonal integrity, inflammation, and muscle-brain communication. METHODS: In this randomized controlled substudy, 40 PwPD were assigned to a multidisciplinary intensive outpatient rehabilitation program (experimental group, EXP; n = 20) or a home-based self-managed intervention (control group, CTRL; n = 20). Assessments were performed at baseline (T0), post-treatment (T1), and 3-month follow-up (T2). Clinical outcomes included motor function (UPDRS-III), cognition (MoCA), and functional status (ADL, IADL). Plasma levels of neurofilament light chain (NFL), irisin, interleukin-6 (IL-6), and soluble IL-6 receptor (sIL-6R) were measured. RESULTS: No significant changes over time or between groups were observed in motor or cognitive outcomes. In contrast, significant biomarker modulation was detected. Irisin levels increased in the EXP group at T1 and T2, while decreasing in the CTRL group (p < 0.01). NFL levels significantly decreased in the EXP group at both time points, whereas an increase was observed at follow-up in the CTRL group. IL-6 remained stable in both groups. sIL-6R levels decreased over time, with a significant group-by-time interaction at T1 (p = 0.038). No significant correlations emerged between clinical outcomes and biomarkers. CONCLUSIONS: Intensive multidisciplinary rehabilitation was associated with significant modulation of circulating biomarkers, despite the absence of clinical changes. Decreased NFL and increased irisin suggest potential neuroprotective and exercise-responsive effects. papers.title: Rotigotine Behenate ameliorates depression in Parkinson's disease through NF-κB-mediated anti-inflammation and BDNF-mediated neuroprotection.
papers.abstract: Depression in Parkinson's disease (DPD) is a prevalent non-motor complication that currently lacks effective targeted therapy. We established a combined MPTP/CUMS model in male C57BL/6 mice, which induced a higher incidence of depression and more stable depressive-like phenotypes than MPTP-only modeling and closely recapitulated clinical DPD pathology. Pearson correlation analysis confirmed severe dopamine (DA) and 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) dysregulation predominantly in the striatum (STR) and prefrontal cortex (PFC), identifying these regions as core DPD lesion sites. Behavioral assays demonstrated that ROTB ameliorated both motor dysfunction and depressive-like behavior and restored regional neurotransmitter balance, whereas fluoxetine-included solely as an efficacy comparator for the depressive-like phenotype-did not improve motor symptoms. Mechanistically, ROTB suppressed NF-κB/NLRP3-mediated neuroinflammation and activated the BDNF/TrkB/PI3K/Akt/GSK-3β cascade, elevating synaptic protein levels and reversing dendritic spine loss. Pharmacological inhibition of the NF-κB pathway with QNZ only partially recapitulated the antidepressant effects of ROTB, indicating the existence of NF-κB-independent protective mechanisms. In summary, ROTB alleviates DPD through NF-κB-mediated anti-inflammation and BDNF-mediated neuroprotection, offering preclinical evidence for DPD therapy.

papers.title: Psychiatric sequelae following STN-DBS in Parkinson's disease: Expanding the debate on DBS-related psychosis.
Adult phenotype of genetically confirmed Dravet syndrome: diagnostic challenges and clinical red flags from a multicenter Polish cohort.
papers.abstract: AIM OF THE STUDY: To characterize the clinical phenotype of adults with clinically diagnosed and genetically confirmed Dravet syndrome (DS), with particular emphasis on seizure evolution, cognitive and motor impairment, and diagnostic delay. CLINICAL RATIONALE FOR THE STUDY: An increasing number of individuals with DS survive into adulthood and require long-term neurological care. However, the adult phenotype differs from the classical childhood presentation and remains underrecognized in adult neurological practice. Recognition of an age-evolving seizure phenotype, together with intellectual disability, gait and postural abnormalities, and extrapyramidal features, may provide important diagnostic clues and prompt molecular testing in previously undiagnosed adults. MATERIAL AND METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective case series of nine adults (six females and three males) fulfilling clinical diagnostic criteria for DS and carrying a pathogenic or likely pathogenic SCN1A variant. Clinical data were obtained from medical records, neurological examinations, seizure diaries, and psychological assessments performed as part of routine care. Seizure history and evolution, status epilepticus, cognitive and communication impairment, motor phenotype, and treatment history were analyzed. RESULTS: The mean age at evaluation was 27.8 years (range 21-37 years). Seizure onset occurred at a mean age of 6 months, whereas the mean age at molecular diagnosis was 13.2 years, corresponding to a mean diagnostic delay of 12.7 years. Febrile seizures occurred in eight of nine patients and persisted beyond the age of 18 years in three. Generalized tonic-clonic seizures persisted into adulthood in all patients, whereas status epilepticus occurred after the age of 18 years in only one. papers.title: Cognitive load and mobility: Within-session repeatability and preliminary group discrimination of a dual-task 10-Meter Walk Test with Stroop in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cognitive-motor interference during gait is commonly observed in individuals with Parkinson's disease (PD) and may contribute to mobility limitations and increased fall risk. Traditional single-task gait measures may underestimate mobility limitations in complex environments. OBJECTIVES: To examine whether integrating a visual Stroop task with the 10-Meter Walk Test (10MWT) differentiates walking performance between individuals with PD and healthy adults, and to evaluate the within-session repeatability of the Stroop-enhanced 10MWT. METHODS: Twenty participants with Parkinson's disease (PwP), 19 healthy older adults, and 19 healthy young adults were included in the complete-case walking analyses involving the 10MWT, Standing Stroop, and Stroop-enhanced 10MWT. Participants with PD additionally completed the TUG-cognitive. Completion times, Stroop errors, and gait dual-task costs were analyzed. Group comparisons were supplemented by sensitivity analyses, and within-session repeatability was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients from three trials. Results: Single-task 10MWT completion times did not differ significantly among groups (p CONCLUSIONS: The Stroop-enhanced 10MWT identified differences in dual-task walking performance between PwP and healthy older adults that were not observed during single-task walking. Its excellent within-session repeatability and preliminary ability to differentiate groups suggest potential utility for assessing cognitive-motor interference in PD. Further studies are needed to establish its validity, between-session reliability, and clinical applicability.

papers.title: Assessing Dysphagia in Parkinson's Disease: Psychometric Properties of the Italian version of the Mann Assessment of Swallowing Ability (MASA-IT).
papers.journal: Folia phoniatrica et logopaedica : official organ of the International Association of Logopedics and Phoniatrics (IALP)
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Dysphagia is a common non-motor symptom of Parkinson's disease (PD), associated with reduced quality of life and increased risk of malnutrition, aspiration pneumonia, and hospitalization. Although several clinical tools are available, few have been specifically investigated in individuals with PD. The Mann Assessment of Swallowing Ability (MASA) is widely used in clinical practice, but evidence supporting its use in this population remains limited. This study investigated the psychometric properties of the Italian version of the Mann Assessment of Swallowing Ability (MASA-IT) in individuals with PD. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 51 individuals with PD underwent swallowing assessment using the MASA-IT. Internal consistency was evaluated using Cronbach's alpha and item-total correlations, while inter-rater and test-retest reliability were examined through intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Exploratory analyses relevant to the convergent aspect of construct validity were conducted by examining correlations between MASA-IT total scores and theoretically related comparator measures, including the Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS), Dysphagia in Parkinson's Disease questionnaire (DYPARK), Mealtime Assessment Tool (MAT), and MDS-UPDRS Part II. RESULTS: MASA-IT showed suboptimal internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.650), good inter-rater reliability (ICC = 0.858, 95% CI 0.751-0.919), and good test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.897, 95% CI 0.820-0.941). Moderate correlations were observed with FOIS (r = 0.481, p < 0.001), DYPARK (r = -0.398, p = 0.004), MAT (r = 0.366, p = 0.008), and MDS-UPDRS Part II (r = -0.448, p = 0.013). Item-level ceiling effects exceeding 15% were found for 22 of the 24 items, three of which were invariant, indicating limited item-level discriminative ability; no ceiling effect was observed for the total score. papers.title: Translation, adaptation and validation of Parkinson's disease quality of life - 39 questionnaire to Yoruba language.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Parkinson's disease quality of life questionnaire (PDQ-39) is a widely accepted measure available in many African languages, none of which is a Nigerian language. This study was aimed at translation and adaptation of the PDQ-39 to Yoruba language of the southwest Nigeria, and assessing the validity and reliability of Yoruba version of PDQ (PDQ-39 (Y)). METHODS: This adaptation followed the American Association of Orthopedic Surgeons guidelines. The English version of PDQ-39 was cross-culturally adapted into Yoruba using forward- and back-translation, expert panel review, pre-testing of pre-final version on 10 patients with PD for cognitive debriefing interview to produce the final PDQ-39(Y). The PDQ-39 and PDQ-39(Y) were administered concurrently on 40 respondents with PD for known-group validity. The PDQ-39(Y) was re-administered on 33 respondents at 14-day interval for test-retest reliability. Respondents' socio-demographic data were also recorded. Socio-demographic variables, PDQ-39 and PDQ-39(Y) scores were summarised using descriptive statistics. Known-group validity was assessed using independent t-test by gender and one-way ANOVA by age and educational level. Pearson's correlation method examined agreement between PDQ-39 and PDQ-39(Y). Internal consistency and test-retest reliability of PDQ-39(Y) were determined by Cronbach's alpha and intra-class correlation coefficient (ICC) respectively. Construct validity was determined through first-order confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). Level of significance was at p < 0.05. RESULTS: The adaptation process revealed experiential and semantic equivalence issues in certain words, which were resolved during the expert panel meeting.
